reason: E3 and E4 directly support the formation of an amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite with Ag nanocrystals and the resulting low friction and wear in a TiNbZr-Ag alloy, but the cited evidence does not address the AlCoCrFeNi system, the specific 7 at% Ag concentration, or the wide temperature range up to 600 °C, leaving key premises about the base alloy and temperature range unsupported.
premises: Ag addition to a HEA can promote in-situ formation of an amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite tribolayer during wear in air
Such a tribolayer reduces friction (COF ~0.09) and wear rate (by ~2 orders of magnitude) compared to the Ag-free alloy
The mechanism involves environmental oxygen reacting with the surface, with Ag segregation aiding nanocrystal formation
The reactive wear protection concept is effective from room temperature up to at least 600 °C
The AlCoCrFeNi HEA system is a suitable base alloy for this Ag-induced reactive wear protection
